description: The Paramahaṃsa Upaniṣad, a saṃnyāsa Upaniṣad, describes the characteristics of the highest renouncer (paramahaṃsa) and the path of knowledge (jñāna); its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Parāśarasmṛti
description: A Dharmaśāstra traditionally attributed to Parāśara, prescribing norms for the Kali age; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Praśna Upaniṣad
description: An Upaniṣad organized around six questions, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Rāmāyaṇa
description: An Itihāsa text with many regional and textual traditions. This record avoids collapsing those traditions into one account.

title: Ṛgveda Saṃhitā
description: The Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, the oldest Vedic collection of 1028 hymns (sūktas) in ten maṇḍalas, dedicated to various deities; its textual structure, metres, and recensions are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rigveda
description: A concise source-aware catalogue overview. This record contains no reproduced scripture or translation.

title: Rudrahṛdaya Upaniṣad
description: The Rudrahṛdaya Upaniṣad, a Śaiva Upaniṣad, identifies Rudra as the supreme reality and the heart (hṛdaya) of all beings; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṣaḍviṃśa Brāhmaṇa
description: The Ṣaḍviṃśa Brāhmaṇa, the twenty-sixth book supplementing the Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa, contains additional ritual material for Sāma Vedic sacrifices; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sāmaveda Āraṇyaka
description: The Sāmaveda Āraṇyakas, associated with the Kauthuma and Jaiminīya Śākhās, contain the Chāndogya Upaniṣad and related forest texts; their content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sāmaveda Saṃhitā
description: The Sāmaveda Saṃhitā is the collection of melodic verses (sāmans) drawn primarily from the Ṛgveda for liturgical chanting; its textual structure and musical notation are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sāmaveda
description: A Vedic collection represented as a source-aware catalogue entry. Its textual and recitational traditions are not treated as identical to those of the other Vedas.

title: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa
description: The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, associated with the Mādhyandina and Kāṇva Śākhās of the Śukla Yajurveda, is one of the most extensive Brāhmaṇas, containing detailed ritual instructions and theological discussions including the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Śiva Purāṇa
description: A major Śaiva Purāṇa presenting Śiva-centered cosmology, theology, and ritual; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad
description: The Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad, associated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, is a theistic Upaniṣad focusing on Rudra/Śiva as the supreme deity; its theistic terminology and bhakti orientation are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Skanda Purāṇa
description: The largest Mahāpurāṇa, centered on Kārttikeya (Skanda), with extensive pilgrimage and temple lore; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Subāla Upaniṣad
description: The Subāla Upaniṣad, associated with the Śukla Yajurveda, is a dialogue between Sage Subāla and Prajāpati on the nature of Brahman, the self, and the universe; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Taittirīya Āraṇyaka
description: The Taittirīya Āraṇyaka, associated with the Taittirīya Śākhā, contains the Taittirīya Upaniṣad and the Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad; its forest-text character and philosophical content are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa
description: The Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, associated with the Taittirīya Śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, provides ritual explanations and theological interpretations of the Saṃhitā mantras; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Taittirīya Saṃhitā
description: The Taittirīya Saṃhitā is the Saṃhitā of the Taittirīya Śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, containing mantras for Vedic rituals; its textual structure and content are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Taittirīya Upaniṣad
description: An Upaniṣad associated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Tārasāra Upaniṣad
description: The Tārasāra Upaniṣad, a Śaiva Upaniṣad, teaches the tāraka-mantra (Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya) as the means to cross the ocean of saṃsāra; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Vāmana Purāṇa
description: A Mahāpurāṇa associated with Viṣṇu's dwarf (vāmana) incarnation, covering cosmology and pilgrimage; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Varāha Purāṇa
description: A Mahāpurāṇa associated with Viṣṇu's boar (varāha) incarnation, focusing on cosmology, ritual, and sacred geography; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Vārttika
description: The Vārttikas of Kātyāyana are critical supplements to Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī, identifying omissions, redundancies, and errors; their textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Vasiṣṭha Dharmasūtra
description: An early Dharmasūtra associated with the Ṛgveda, prescribing duties for the four varṇas and āśramas; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Vāsudeva Upaniṣad
description: The Vāsudeva Upaniṣad, a Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad associated with the Saṃhitā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, focuses on Vāsudeva (Kṛṣṇa) as the supreme deity and the dvādaśākṣara mantra; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Vāyu Purāṇa
description: A Mahāpurāṇa traditionally narrated by the wind-god Vāyu, covering creation, genealogy, and geography; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Viṣṇu Purāṇa
description: One of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas, presenting Viṣṇu-centered cosmology, genealogy, and theology; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Mahābhāṣya
description: The Mahābhāṣya of Patañjali is the major commentary on Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī, providing extensive grammatical analysis and philosophical discussion; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Vyāsasmṛti
description: A Dharmaśāstra attributed to Vyāsa, covering ritual, penance, and social duties; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Yājñavalkyasmṛti
description: A major Dharmaśāstra noted for its systematic organization of law, procedure, and penance; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Yajurveda Saṃhitā
description: The Yajurveda Saṃhitā, the collection of prose mantras (yajus) for ritual use, transmitted in Kṛṣṇa (Taittirīya, Maitrāyaṇīya, Kaṭha, Kāpiṣṭhala) and Śukla (Mādhyandina, Kāṇva) recensions; its textual structure is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Yajurveda
description: A Vedic collection represented here as a concise catalogue record. Its recensions and associated textual layers require context-specific study.

title: Yāska's Nirukta
description: The Nirukta, attributed to Yāska, is the Vedāṅga of etymology and semantic interpretation, providing explanations of obscure Vedic terms through derivations and glosses; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Yogacūḍāmaṇi Upaniṣad
description: The Yogacūḍāmaṇi Upaniṣad, a Yoga Upaniṣad, describes the chakras, nāḍīs, kuṇḍalinī, and the practice of rāja-yoga leading to samādhi; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Yogatattva Upaniṣad
description: The Yogatattva Upaniṣad, a Yoga Upaniṣad, classifies yoga into mantra, laya, haṭha, and rāja yoga, and describes the four stages of yoga practice; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Badrinātha Temple
description: The Badrinātha Temple at Badrinath, Uttarakhand, one of the four Dhāmas and a major Viṣṇu pilgrimage site; its seasonal opening, architecture, and Ādi Śaṅkara association are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Belur Chennakesava Temple
description: The Chennakesava Temple at Belur, Karnataka, a Hoysala masterpiece with intricate soapstone sculptures, built by Viṣṇuvardhana; its architecture, iconography, and UNESCO World Heritage nomination are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bṛhadīśvara Temple (Tanjore)
description: The Bṛhadīśvara Temple at Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, a UNESCO World Heritage site built by Rājarāja I; its architecture, inscriptions, and bronze sculptures are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Dvārakā Temple (Dvārakādhīśa)
description: The Dvārakādhīśa Temple at Dvārakā, Gujarat, one of the four Dhāmas and a major Kṛṣṇa pilgrimage site; its history and submerged city traditions are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Guruvāyūr Temple (Kṛṣṇa)
description: The Guruvāyūr Temple in Kerala, a major Kṛṣṇa pilgrimage site with distinctive Kerala architecture and elephant traditions; its daily rituals and festival calendar are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Halebidu Hoysaleswara Temple
description: The Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu, Karnataka, a twin Hoysala temple dedicated to Śiva, renowned for its extensive sculptural program; its architecture, iconography, and UNESCO World Heritage nomination are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Jagannātha Temple, Purī
description: The Jagannātha Temple at Purī, Odisha, one of the four Dhāmas; its distinctive deities, Ratha Yātrā, and temple administration are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Kāñcīpuram Temples
description: The temple city of Kāñcīpuram, Tamil Nadu, with major Śaiva (Ekāmranātha, Kāmākṣī) and Vaiṣṇava (Varadarāja) temples; its history as a Śaṅkara maṭha center is represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Kāśī Viśvanātha Temple
description: The Viśvanātha Temple at Kāśī (Vārāṇasī), Uttar Pradesh, one of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas and a major Śiva pilgrimage center; its history of destruction/rebuilding and Ghats are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Kedārnātha Temple
description: The Kedārnātha Temple at Kedarnath, Uttarakhand, one of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas; its high-altitude location, seasonal access, and Śaṅkara association are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Khajuraho Temples
description: The Khajuraho group of temples, Madhya Pradesh, built by the Chandela dynasty (9th–12th centuries), famous for their erotic sculptures and Nagara architecture; a UNESCO World Heritage site represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Konark Sun Temple
description: The Sun Temple at Konark, Odisha, a 13th-century chariot-shaped temple dedicated to Sūrya, a UNESCO World Heritage site; its architecture, erotic sculptures, and astronomical alignment are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mīnākṣī Amman Temple
description: The Mīnākṣī Amman Temple at Madurai, Tamil Nadu, a major Śaiva-Śākta pilgrimage site with towering gopurams and tank; its history, architecture, and festival traditions are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Pāṇḍharpur Temple (Viṭṭhala)
description: The Viṭṭhala Temple at Pāṇḍharpur, Maharashtra, the center of the Vārkarī tradition; its annual Palkhi pilgrimage and Nāmadeva/Tukārām associations are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Rāmeśvaram Temple
description: The Rāmanāthasvāmi Temple at Rāmeśvaram, Tamil Nadu, one of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas and a Dhāma; its corridors, tīrthas, and Rāma association are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Sabarimala Temple (Ayyappa)
description: The Ayyappa Temple at Sabarimala, Kerala, a major pilgrimage site with a distinctive 41-day vrata and seasonal opening; its history, forest setting, and Makaravilakku are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Somnāth Temple
description: The Somnāth Temple at Prabhas Patan, Gujarat, the first of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas; its history of repeated destruction and reconstruction is represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Śrīraṅgam Temple (Ranganathaswamy)
description: The Ranganātha Temple at Śrīraṅgam, Tamil Nadu, the largest functioning temple complex in India and a major Vaiṣṇava pilgrimage site; its seven enclosures and Āḻvār associations are represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Tirupati Balaji (Veṅkaṭeśvara Temple)
description: The Venkaṭeśvara Temple at Tirumala, Andhra Pradesh, one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in India; its history, architecture, and administration are complex and represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Darśana
description: A classification for philosophical systems represented as distinct schools rather than one homogeneous position.

title: Deity traditions
description: A classification for deity-centered textual and living traditions without imposing theological hierarchy.

title: Festival traditions
description: A classification for festivals and observances whose forms vary by region, community and tradition.

title: Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava tradition
description: A Vaiṣṇava tradition traditionally said to originate in Bengal, centered on Kṛṣṇa-bhakti and the teachings of Caitanya Mahāprabhu; its theological and ritual distinctives are represented here without sectarian ranking.

title: Liṅgāyat tradition
description: A Śaiva tradition traditionally said to originate in Karnataka with distinct institutional and ritual forms; represented here without conflating it with other Śaiva lineages.

title: Practice
description: A portal classification for lived practices, not a claim that all communities practice in the same way.

title: Sanskrit
description: A language and literary domain represented here through texts, terms, grammar and transmission rather than as a single uniform tradition.

title: Śaiva traditions
description: A broad category for Śiva-centered traditions with diverse textual, ritual, and regional forms; not presented as a single organization.

title: Śākta traditions
description: A broad category for Devī-centered traditions with diverse textual, ritual, and regional forms; not presented as a single organization.

title: Śruti
description: A classification used for bodies of Vedic literature and related textual traditions; its use is contextual rather than a claim that all traditions structure texts identically.

title: Smārta traditions
description: A tradition associated with the worship of five deities (pañcāyatana) and the Advaita Vedānta framework; its boundaries and practices vary regionally.

title: Śrī Vaiṣṇava tradition
description: A Vaiṣṇava tradition associated with Rāmānuja and the Viśiṣṭādvaita framework; its temple and monastic institutions are distinct from other Vaiṣṇava lineages.

title: Upaniṣads
description: A broad category for Upaniṣadic texts, represented with attention to differences among texts, recensions and interpretations.

title: Vaiṣṇava traditions
description: A broad category for traditions centered on Viṣṇu or related forms; it contains diverse lineages and should not be treated as one organization.

title: Vedāṅga
description: A classification for auxiliary disciplines associated with Vedic study; its individual domains have distinct histories and textual materials.
